entry.title: La Capte Beach, Hyeres
entry.summary: La Capte is a long beach of fine sand on the Giens peninsula near Hyeres, with pine trees behind and calm, shallow water. The steady wind makes it a favourite spot for windsurfing and kitesurfing, and the water stays shallow for a long way out.

entry.title: Kerfissien Beach, Cleder
entry.summary: Kerfissien is a wide beach of pale sand in Cleder, on the north coast of Finistere, dotted with pink granite boulders and backed by dunes. The tides change the beach a lot, and at low tide a large flat shore opens up for walking.

entry.title: Plage des Blancs-Sablons, Le Conquet
entry.summary: Les Blancs-Sablons is a wide beach of pale sand near Le Conquet at the western tip of Brittany, with dunes behind and the open Atlantic in front. The waves suit surfers, and the water is cold, so most visitors come for walks, views and the big sky.

entry.title: Praia do Magoito, Sintra
entry.summary: Praia do Magoito is a small sandy cove between golden sandstone cliffs on the Sintra coast, west of Lisbon. The Atlantic waves are strong and the water is cool, and the dramatic cliffs make it a popular spot for walks and sunset views.

entry.title: Praia de Sao Torpes, Sines
entry.summary: Praia de Sao Torpes is a sandy beach on the Alentejo coast near Sines, sheltered by a long breakwater that keeps the water calmer than on neighbouring beaches. Dunes and low scrub run behind, and the water is clear.

entry.title: Praia da Mareta, Sagres
entry.summary: Praia da Mareta is a sandy beach below the ochre cliffs of Sagres in the western Algarve, close to the village centre. The beach is sheltered from some winds by the cliffs, and the water is cool and clear, with the Sagres fortress nearby.

entry.title: Omis Beach
entry.summary: Omis is a small Dalmatian town at the mouth of the Cetina river, wedged between steep limestone mountains and the sea. The town beach is made of pebbles with clear water, and the setting makes it one of the most dramatic on the Adriatic.

entry.title: Gradac Beach, Makarska Riviera
entry.summary: Gradac is a pebble beach town at the southern end of the Makarska Riviera, with a long promenade, clear water and the Biokovo mountains rising steeply behind. It is quieter than the resorts further north and has a relaxed, family feel.

entry.title: Soline Beach, Brela
entry.summary: Soline is a pebble beach beside the village of Brela on the Makarska Riviera, shaded by pines, with clear turquoise water and the Biokovo mountains behind. It sits next to the better-known Punta Rata beach and is a little quieter.

entry.title: Cupabia Beach, Corsica
entry.summary: Cupabia is a long, pale beach in the Gulf of Valinco in south-west Corsica, with a Genoese watchtower close by and maquis-covered hills behind. The water is clear and shallow, and the beach is much quieter than the resorts in the south-east of the island.

entry.title: Pescoluse Beach, Salento
entry.summary: Pescoluse is a long beach of fine white sand on the Ionian coast of Salento, often called the Maldives of Salento for its shallow, clear water and pale dunes. The sea stays calm and shallow for a long way out, which suits families.

entry.title: Porto Pollo Beach, Palau
entry.summary: Porto Pollo is a pair of bays on either side of a narrow isthmus in northern Sardinia, near Palau. The water is shallow and clear, and steady winds make it one of the best places in Italy for windsurfing and kitesurfing.

entry.title: Cala en Porter, Menorca
entry.summary: Cala en Porter is a cove of fine white sand in a narrow ravine on the south coast of Menorca, with turquoise water and tall cliffs on both sides. Houses climb the western cliff, and a cave known for its sunset bar sits on the opposite side.

entry.title: Playa de Carnota
entry.summary: Playa de Carnota is one of the longest beaches in Galicia, a wide stretch of fine pale sand on the Costa da Morte, with the granite slopes of Monte Pindo rising behind. A lagoon and wetland sit behind the dunes, and the beach stays uncrowded outside August.

entry.title: Playa de Zahora, Barbate
entry.summary: Zahora is a long, open beach of golden sand on the Cadiz coast, backed by pine woods and low cliffs. The Atlantic sea is clear, the wind keeps the beach fresh, and it is much quieter than the resorts of the Costa del Sol.

entry.title: Los Canos de Meca Beach
entry.summary: Los Canos de Meca is a laid-back beach village in Barbate, Cadiz, with sandy beaches backed by cliffs and pine woods. The Trafalgar lighthouse stands on the cape nearby, and the Atlantic water is clear, with waves that suit surfers.

entry.title: Agia Roumeli Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Agia Roumeli is a small village on the south coast of Crete with a long pebble beach, reached on foot through the Samaria Gorge or by ferry. There is no road to the village, so the beach feels remote, and the sea is deep blue below tall mountains.

entry.title: Frangokastello Beach, Crete
entry.summary: Frangokastello is a long beach of pale sand on the south coast of Crete, beside a square Venetian castle with the White Mountains rising behind. The sea is shallow and clear, and the area is much quieter than the big resorts on the north coast.

entry.title: Fasolou Beach, Sifnos
entry.summary: Fasolou is a small sandy bay close to the fishing hamlet of Faros on Sifnos, with clear shallow water and low dry hills around it. It is a quiet spot reached by a short walk from Faros, and the hamlet has tavernas near the shore.

entry.title: Pollonia Beach, Milos
entry.summary: Pollonia is a small fishing village on the north-east tip of Milos, with a calm sandy beach beside the harbour and shallow water that suits children. The island of Kimolos sits across the narrow strait, and ferries cross from the port.

entry.title: Pefkoulia Beach, Lefkada
entry.summary: Pefkoulia is a long beach of golden sand and pebbles on the west coast of Lefkada, below steep green hills near Agios Nikitas. The sea is deep turquoise, and the beach opens to the Ionian sea with good late-afternoon light.

entry.title: Livadakia Beach, Serifos
entry.summary: Livadakia is a curved bay of sand and fine pebbles just beside the port of Livadi on Serifos, with tamarisk trees and low brown hills around it. The water is clear and calm, and the bay is a short walk from the ferry quay.

entry.title: Psili Ammos Beach, Serifos
entry.summary: Psili Ammos is a quiet cove of fine pale sand on the south-east coast of Serifos, with shallow turquoise water and a line of tamarisk trees behind the beach. Rocky headlands close the bay on both sides, and the beach feels remote even in summer.

entry.title: Praia da Vieira, Marinha Grande
entry.summary: Praia da Vieira is a wide beach of golden sand on the central Atlantic coast of Portugal, with traditional fishing boats pulled up on the sand and the Leiria pine forest behind. The sea is strong and cool, so swimming is best in the lifeguarded area.

entry.title: Pramousquier Beach
entry.summary: Pramousquier is a quiet sandy bay between Le Lavandou and Cavaliere on the Var coast, backed by pine woods and low hills. The water is clear and calm, and the beach is much less busy than the big resorts nearby.

entry.title: Biodola Beach, Elba
entry.summary: Biodola is a wide bay of pale sand and fine gravel on the north coast of Elba, west of Portoferraio, with turquoise water and green hills on both sides. The water is shallow and clear, and a few hotels stand behind the beach.

entry.title: Playa de El Sardinero, Santander
entry.summary: El Sardinero is the main beach area of Santander in Cantabria, made up of two wide sandy bays divided by a rocky point. A seafront of elegant belle epoque buildings, gardens and the casino stands behind the sand.

entry.title: Playa del Postiguet, Alicante
entry.summary: Playa del Postiguet is the main city beach of Alicante, a curved stretch of golden sand below the Santa Barbara castle on its rock. The water is shallow and warm in summer, and a palm-lined promenade runs along the back of the beach.

entry.title: Copacabana Beach, Dubrovnik
entry.summary: Copacabana is a long pebble beach on the Babin Kuk peninsula in Dubrovnik, with clear water and a lively beach scene. Beach bars, water sports and hotels sit behind it, and the old town is a short bus ride away.

entry.title: Livadi Beach, Astypalaia
entry.summary: Livadi is the main beach of Astypalaia, a green valley bay with pebbles and sand below the whitewashed Chora and its Venetian castle. Tamarisk trees give shade, and a few tavernas sit just behind the beach.
